title: Google Chrome 153 Fixes 42 Security Flaws, Including Critical WebGL and Use-After-Free Bugs
content_md: Google has released Chrome 153 to the Stable channel, addressing 42 security vulnerabilities across the browser’s rendering, JavaScript, graphics, extension, authentication, and platform components. The update is rolling out as version 153.0.8010.47/.48 for Windows and macOS, and version 153.0.8010.47 for Linux. The September 15, 2026 release contains three critical-severity flaws, including an out-of-bounds read in WebGL and two use-after-free vulnerabilities affecting Chrome Internals and Workers. Google Chrome 153 Fixes 42 Security Flaws The most severe issue, tracked as CVE-2026-91726, is an out-of-bounds read vulnerability in WebGL. WebGL exposes GPU-accelerated graphics capabilities to web content, making memory-safety defects in this component particularly important in browser attack scenarios. A successful exploit could potentially allow a malicious website to trigger unexpected memory access within the browser’s graphics-processing path. Chrome 153 also resolves CVE-2026-91721, a use-after-free flaw in Internals, and CVE-2026-91749, a use-after-free issue in Workers. Use-after-free bugs occur when software continues accessing memory after releasing it. In browsers, attackers commonly attempt to exploit these defects through crafted web content to cause crashes, corrupt memory, or potentially achieve code execution within a compromised browser process.
